conviction_note: Mild negative lean (p_up 44) on a 7-point absolute move. Sprouts printed the same July-September months on Oct 29 at -0.9% comps against its own -0.5% to +1.5% guide. NGVC's FY guide needs Q4 comps of about 2.6-4.6%, and Street Q4 EPS of $0.56 sits at the top of the $0.52-0.56 the guide implies. Three things pull p_up toward 50: the stock is already -18% over 20 days and -9.5% over 5, short interest is 7.7% of float at about 7.9 days to cover, and Grocery Outlet's value-channel traffic was positive. Findings sum -1.7 against a scaled -0.84; they are measured separately and not fitted.
bar: Q4 FY26 (Jul-Sep 2026) diluted EPS consensus $0.56 from Chartmill and FXEmpire (3 analysts, revenue $359.0-359.7m); Benzinga $0.57 / $352.1m, possibly stale. Company FY26 guide (8-K 2026-08-06, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001547459/000143774926026263/ex_999263.htm): diluted EPS $2.07-2.11 and daily average comps +1.5-2.0%. With Q1-Q3 EPS of $0.49+$0.58+$0.48 = $1.55, the guide implies Q4 EPS $0.52-0.56, so consensus is at the top of the range. FY consensus $2.11-2.14 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-11, https://finviz.com/news/421344/natural-grocers-must-prove-its-margin-slip-was-a-one-off-as-guidance-points-to-the-high-end; Chartmill). With Q1-Q3 comps of 1.7/0.5/1.2, the guide implies Q4 comps of about 2.6-4.6% against a 4.2% prior-year Q4. FY27: no company guide exists yet. The only consensus found is WallStreetZen's $2.31 average ($2.13-2.51) with revenue near $1.43b; that is a single thin source, so the guidance finding is capped small. Consensus sources: https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/NGVC/estimates, https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/ngvc/earnings
positioning_check: Short interest: Chartmill, settlement 2026-10-15, about 990.7k shares, 7.67% of float, 7.94 days to cover (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/NGVC/ownership/short-interest). Days to cover is elevated because turnover is thin (102k shares a day over 20 days) and the float is small, with the Isely family as a controlling 13D group. Older reads: DTC 4.19 (2026-06-30, curvedtrading), 4.86 (2026-03-13, equibles); borrow fee about 0.4%. Options: unusable, with 62 contracts of total open interest and put/call OI 2.1, so there is no skew number. Tape into the print: -9.49% over 5 days, -18.38% over 20 days, 21.7% off the 52-week high and 11.4% off the low. Spot was $29.15 on 2026-11-11, $28.45 on 11-16 and $26.42 at the seal. No news source explains the last-week drop; the only company filing that week is the Texas reincorporation 8-K. The short is moderately crowded relative to liquidity and the stock has de-rated into the print, which argues for shrinking negatives.

findings.finding: Sprouts reported on 2026-10-29 for the quarter ended 2026-09-27, the same July-September months as NGVC's fiscal Q4. Comps were -0.9%, below its own Q3 guide of -0.5% to +1.5%, with transactions -3.3% and basket +2.5%. It guided Q4 comps -2% to -4% and cut FY comps to about -1.7%. Lapping a 5.9% prior-year quarter (10.2% the quarter before), its two-year stack slowed from about 9.2 to about 5.0. NGVC's FY guide of +1.5-2.0% needs its one-year comp to accelerate from Q3's +1.2% to about +2.6-4.6% in Q4 while lapping 4.2%. Sprouts got no lapping benefit in the same months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NGVC trades on comps and margin. In Aug 2026, comps of +1.2% with a trimmed comp guide and a 60bp gross-margin decline gave -12.54%. In May 2026, comps of +0.5% with the comp guide cut from 1.5-4.0% to 1.5-2.5% gave -4.86%. Five of the last seven prints moved down (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. NGVC fell from about $32 to the high $20s after Oct 29. But the 3-analyst Q4 consensus still reads $0.56 EPS and $352-360m revenue, the top of the guide-implied range and about +5-7% sales growth. Revisions would have taken it to the guide midpoint or below if the read-through had been carried into estimates. NGVC has said nothing since Aug 6.
findings.independence: A peer, not a counterparty. The link is the same natural and organic channel and overlapping Western/Mountain states (CO, AZ, TX, UT). The Shelby Report (https://theshelbyreport.com/2026/10/29/sprouts-comps-dip-0-9-in-q3-as-grocer-opens-record-15-stores/) and Supermarket News confirm the figures from the same release. Against it: Sprouts named a cyclospora (produce) disruption and new-store cannibalisation that are its own; NGVC's Apr-Jun comp of +1.2% beat Sprouts' -1.0% by 2.2 points; and Placer.ai put Sprouts same-store visits at about -0.1% in Q3 (https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/sprouts-finds-steadier-ground-in-q3-2026).

findings.finding: Street Q4 EPS of $0.56 (Chartmill and FXEmpire agree) is at the top of the $0.52-0.56 implied by NGVC's FY26 guide. Q3's reported $0.48 (vs $0.50) included a $2m business-interruption insurance recovery, about $0.06-0.07 a share after tax on about 23m shares, so the underlying Q3 was about $0.41-0.42, about 16% below last year. Q4 must reach +2% to +10% year on year against $0.51, with one fewer selling day (Labor Day closure) and about $0.08 of pre-opening costs (Earnings Whispers preview).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS and margin quality: Q3 FY26 at $0.48 vs $0.50, with gross margin -60bp, gave -12.54%. Q1 FY26 at $0.49 vs $0.43, an EPS beat with gross margin -40bp, gave -2.22%. Beats have not been bought; margin slips have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The insurance recovery is in the release and in trade coverage (https://www.supermarketnews.com/finance/natural-grocers-q3-success-comes-with-a-hidden-downside), but consensus still sits at the top of the guide. If the market expected the underlying run-rate to persist, estimates would sit near $0.52-0.54. Sell-side coverage is thin (about 3 analysts) and estimates appear not to have moved since August.
findings.independence: Same company document as the guide arithmetic. Q1/Q2 EPS come from the company's own releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001547459/000143774926015580/ex_957290.htm). The Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/421344/natural-grocers-must-prove-its-margin-slip-was-a-one-off-as-guidance-points-to-the-high-end) independently says the Street is at the top of the range with little cushion. Against it: the preview expects shrink to normalise now the ERP upgrade is complete, and management kept the $2.07 low end in August.

findings.finding: This release carries the first FY2027 guide. The only FY27 consensus found is WallStreetZen's average $2.31 EPS ($2.13-2.51) and about $1.43b revenue, roughly +10% EPS and +5% sales on FY26's $2.07-2.11. Last year's first guide (Nov 2025) was $2.00-2.15, a midpoint of +3.75% on FY25's $2.00, and FY26 comps have run about 1.5%. A similar-shaped FY27 range (midpoint about $2.15-2.20) would land below that consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 first FY26 guide: EPS $2.00-2.15 against $1.95 consensus, above the Street, and the stock still fell -5.04%. Guide trims in May and Aug 2026 gave -4.86% and -12.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock's -18% over 20 days may already discount a soft guide, which is why this is small. The visible tell would be FY27 estimates near $2.15-2.20; the one public figure is still $2.31, and the bar is single-sourced, so the finding is capped.
findings.independence: Inference from the company's own guide history (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1547459/000143774925035859/ex_890501.htm, 2025-11-20) against a single, thin consensus source. Store growth of 4-5% a year (management, Aug 2026) and a 9.7% private-label mix could support a higher guide.

findings.finding: Grocery Outlet reported on 2026-11-10 for the quarter ended 2026-10-03, closely overlapping NGVC's fiscal Q4. Comps were +0.5% with transactions +2.4%, the first positive comp after three negative quarters, and it raised its FY comp guide to +0.2-0.4% from -0.5-0.0%. Value-positioned grocery gained traffic in July-September. NGVC markets itself as the 'value leader' in natural and organic ('Even More Affordable Prices').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NGVC's transaction count was -1.8% in Q3 FY26 and +1.0% in Q1 FY26. No NGVC print has been isolated on a peer read.
findings.why_not_priced: Released after NGVC last spoke, and the stock fell further after Nov 11, so it has not been read as an NGVC positive. It is a weak, different-format peer, which caps the size.
findings.independence: A peer proxy from a different format (closeout/discount). It cuts against the Sprouts finding; trade coverage at https://www.supermarketnews.com/finance/grocery-outlet-returns-to-positive-comparable-store-sales-in-third-quarter.

findings.finding: UNFI's natural segment, the distributor channel serving independent and natural grocers, grew about 6.6% year on year to $4.26bn in its fiscal Q4, ended about 2026-08-01 and overlapping NGVC's May-July. Natural-channel product demand at wholesale was still growing mid-year.
findings.why_not_priced: Released Sept 8 and widely available, so largely priced. It covers mostly May-July and includes new-customer wins and inflation, so it is a weak transmission to NGVC's August-September.
findings.independence: A channel proxy from a different company than Sprouts or Grocery Outlet. UNFI also guided its own Q1 FY27 sales lower (https://www.grocerydive.com/news/unfi-earnings-fourth-quarter-2026-grocery-wholesale-retail/829758/), which partly offsets it.

findings.finding: BLS food-at-home CPI slowed to +2.2% year on year in August and +1.8% in September 2026 (-0.1% month on month in September). NGVC's Q3 comp of +1.2% came entirely from basket size (+3.1%) while transactions fell 1.8%, so less price help in the back half of the quarter makes the needed Q4 acceleration harder.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26: a basket-driven comp with falling traffic gave -12.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro series, mostly priced. Its link to NGVC's natural/organic basket (supplements, private label) is unconfirmed, so it is small.
findings.independence: A macro proxy; August reading at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_08122026.htm. Not confirmed by the company.

findings.finding: Short interest was 7.67% of float at 7.94 days to cover (2026-10-15), up from 4.2-4.9 days earlier in 2026. The stock enters the print -18.4% over 20 days and -9.5% over 5 days with $2.7m of daily turnover, so an in-line or better print, or a reasonable FY27 guide, has a covering mechanism on a thin float.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2025: +30.24% on a beat with a raised guide, the name's one squeeze-scale reaction (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not news. If the market had priced the downside fully the short would have covered. It is filed small because 7.7% is moderate, not the 18-23% that squeezed in the lessons sample.
findings.independence: The days-to-cover trend comes from older reads at equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/ngvc/shortinterest) and curvedtrading (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/ngvc/).

findings.finding: The Nov 5, 2026 call-date release states 175 stores in 22 states, against 169 stores in 21 states at Mar 31, 2026. FY26 openings reached the 6-7 guide (first Wisconsin store in Q3), and management said all six 2026 openings rank among its strongest opening-day sales. The 4-5% unit growth that feeds the FY27 guide is on track.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Store counts have not been an isolated driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside what the company guided, so close to 0. It supports net sales but adds pre-opening costs to Q4.

findings.finding: NGVC raised its quarterly dividend with last year's Q4 release (2025-11-20: $0.12 to $0.15, +25%). The current rate is $0.15 and nine-month dividends were $10.4m; another raise at this print would follow the pattern.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025: a 25% dividend raise alongside the first guide gave -5.04%. It did not drive the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The pattern is public, so a raise is largely expected; filed small.
findings.independence: Dividend detail in the Q3 FY26 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001547459/000143774926026263/ex_999263.htm).

findings.finding: Management said Q4 FY26 has one fewer selling day because of a Labor Day closure, with most sales expected to shift to adjacent days. Daily-average comps are unaffected; reported net sales lose up to about 1% of a 92-day quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed on the call and inside the guide, so close to 0. It matters only if the $352-360m revenue consensus ignores it.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-11) repeats it.

findings.finding: NGVC reincorporated from Delaware to Texas, effective 2026-11-16 10:59 pm CT (8-K 2026-11-17, Items 3.03/5.03). It was approved by majority written consent (8-K 5.07 on 2026-09-15, DEF 14C on 2026-10-20). The company reports no change to business, management or assets beyond conversion costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. It took effect the session before the -7% slide from $28.45 to $26.42, but there is no evidence it caused it.
findings.why_not_priced: A governance item announced since September; it does not bear on the quarter or the guide, so it is 0.

baseline_tension: No skew exists. The negative lean agrees with the -18% 20-day run-up and the 5-of-7 down reaction history, so much of it is likely in the price. Short interest at 7.9 days to cover cuts against it, which is why p_up is 44 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the FY27 guidance finding rests on a single thin consensus source (WallStreetZen), so it was capped from -0.8 to -0.5. The Q4 EPS bar has two agreeing sources plus the company guide, so finding 2 stands.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): finding 2 trimmed from -1.0 to -0.9. p_up moved from 43 to 44; the short-interest finding stays at +0.5.

Lesson 'a peer's print after the company last spoke leaves consensus stale' (what has worked): the Sprouts finding stays at -1.2 and is not shrunk further, since its counterweights are already reflected in its size.
Lesson 1 (reaction function): checked. The name sells beats and margin slips, which is consistent with the negative lean; no further change, to avoid double-applying.
